findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Require the ADR to document the shared-namespace collision hazard: while `RemoteRef.instance` is unpopulated, all `jira-` prefixed records share one undifferentiated namespace, so running multiple Jira-family deployments against the same store before rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e is resolved is UNSAFE — add an explicit 'do not run two Jira-family instances against the same store until this gap is closed' warning to both the ADR and `docs/user-guide.md`.
evidence: Plan states: 'State it as the INTENDED design with the gap named and tracked ([rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e]), or a future reader will build on a field nothing populates.'
Plan requires the ADR to 'not assert that deployments are distinguished by it as though that were existing reality.'
Neither the Approach section nor any AC line requires the ADR to enumerate the collision/indistinguishability consequence for the shared `jira-` id namespace while the gap persists.
ABSENCE: No AC line requires documenting what happens to the store when two Jira-family instances write `jira-` prefixed records simultaneously before `RemoteRef.instance` is implemented.
findings.finding: The plan requires the ADR to name `RemoteRef.instance` as unbuilt, but does not require documenting the concrete shared-state hazard that follows from that gap: while `RemoteRef.instance` is unpopulated, all Jira-family deployments share the same `jira` creation channel and `jira-` id-prefix namespace with no per-deployment disambiguation, so records written by two concurrently-reconciled Jira instances (e.g., Cloud + DC) would be indistinguishable in the store. The full CREATE/CONSUME/COLLISION lifecycle of this shared namespace is left undescribed.
findings.location: Approach section — RemoteRef.instance bullet; AC item 'the ADR describes RemoteRef.instance as INTENDED design'
scenarios: An operator runs Jira Cloud reconciliation AND Jira DC reconciliation against the same rebar store before epic `be74` / ticket rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e lands; records from both instances share the `jira-` prefix and are indistinguishable, causing silent data collisions or incorrect deduplication.

A future maintainer reading the ADR sees 'intended design, gap tracked' but no description of the collision risk, and concludes it is safe to add a second Jira-family deployment before the gap is closed.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an AC item: 'The ADR and `docs/user-guide.md` explicitly warn that operating more than one Jira-family backend against the same store simultaneously is unsupported until `RemoteRef.instance` is populated (rebar:6a91-7429-e521-4a2e), and describe the collision risk (indistinguishable `jira-` namespaced records) that would result.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Amend the required ADR framing of [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9] to accurately distinguish the two finding categories: (1) seam architecture converged with mature OSS patterns, AND (2) one must-fix data-correctness bug was found (`recover_pending` + DC index lag → duplicate creates, tracked as [rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03]), which is NOT an operational-edge tuning item — the ADR must name it explicitly so future readers cannot conclude the adapter is gap-free.
evidence: Plan text: 'every gap found was instead in OPERATIONAL EDGES that only appear against a differently-configured instance — index lag, server-side pagination caps, admin-toggled rate limiting, screen configuration, project moves'

558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9 session log, first finding: '[rebar:21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03] DC INDEX LAG MAKES recover_pending CREATE DUPLICATE ISSUES… This is the ONLY finding in the whole review where rebar writes wrong data rather than reading incomplete data. Ranked must-fix.'
The session log explicitly distinguishes this finding from the operational-edge category: 'must-fix' vs. the 'filed for follow-up' items (rate limiting, project moves, etc.)
findings.finding: The plan requires the ADR to state that 'every gap found [in the OSS comparison] was instead in OPERATIONAL EDGES that only appear against a differently-configured instance.' This framing is only partially true: ticket [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9]'s session log explicitly identifies one MUST-FIX data-correctness defect (21fc-51d7-90ca-4a03: DC index lag makes `recover_pending` create duplicate issues) that is not an operational-edge tuning item but a logical correctness bug under a well-documented Jira DC behaviour. If the ADR records only the 'operational edges' framing, a future reader inheriting this code — particularly when deciding whether to extend the DC adapter or retire it — will not know a duplicate-write defect was discovered and will build on a false 'architecture held up cleanly' premise.
findings.location: Approach section / Acceptance Criteria: 'the ADR records the OSS-comparison finding [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9]: the seam ARCHITECTURE converged… and every gap found was instead in OPERATIONAL EDGES'
scenarios: A future maintainer reads the ADR and concludes the DC adapter is production-ready with only configuration-sensitivity gaps, then deploys it to a customer with index lag (lagging DC cluster is common in large self-hosted deployments), triggering duplicate issue creation.

Epic be74 (GitHub Issues) authors read the 'seam architecture held up; gaps were operational edges' summary and do not look for analogous logical correctness bugs in the GitHub adapter's recovery path.
findings.suggested_fix: In the AC that requires recording the OSS comparison finding, add a clause: 'and records that the session log also identified one data-correctness defect (21fc: DC index lag causes duplicate creates in the `recover_pending` path) that is not an operational-edge tuning item and is tracked for a future fix — the ADR must not conflate this with the operational-edge findings or omit it.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify whether the pycontribs/jira `token_auth` + stale-JSESSIONID 401 regression (issue #1904) is mitigated in `build_client_from_settings`, and either add the mitigation or record the failure mode as an accepted operational edge in the ADR alongside the OSS-comparison findings.
evidence: pycontribs/jira issue #1904: 'The Jira client initially works with token auth but eventually begins failing with a 401. A key part of the error response is os_authType was "any" and an invalid cookie was sent.' — Atlassian support recommended disabling cookies on outgoing requests.
Plan's Approach section: 'the `pycontribs/jira` dependency, why it is extra-gated' — lists what the ADR must record about the dependency, but does not mention this operational failure mode.

OSS comparison ticket 558e: records operational edges (index lag, server-side pagination caps, admin-toggled rate limiting, screen configuration, project moves) but does NOT include the token_auth+session-cookie 401 regression.
`build_client_from_settings` at transport.py:95: `return jira_cls(server=settings.url, token_auth=settings.pat, options=options or None)` — no cookie-disabling option present.

Plan AC: 'the ADR records the OSS-comparison finding [rebar:558e]: the seam ARCHITECTURE converged … and every gap found was instead in OPERATIONAL EDGES' — the session-cookie 401 is exactly such an operational edge but is absent from the gap list.
findings.finding: A known pycontribs/jira bug — `token_auth` mode can fail with intermittent 401s when a stale JSESSIONID cookie is sent alongside the Bearer Authorization header (github.com/pycontribs/jira issue #1904, confirmed open as of late 2024) — is unaddressed in the plan. The ADR is required to record the dependency justification and operational edges of the DC adapter, but neither the Approach section, the dependency justification AC, nor the OSS-comparison AC directs the author to note this failure mode or its mitigation (disabling cookie persistence in the JIRA client options). The current `build_client_from_settings` constructs `jira.JIRA(token_auth=...)` with no cookie-suppression option. This is a post-deployment operational hazard that the ADR should record alongside the rate-limiting and screen-configuration edges the OSS comparison already surfaces.
findings.location: Approach — 'the `pycontribs/jira` dependency, why it is extra-gated'; AC for OSS-comparison finding [rebar:558e-55ce-d9f1-4fa9]; `src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/adapters/jira_datacenter/transport.py` `build_client_from_settings`
scenarios: A long-running DC reconcile session (multi-hour batch or recurring daemon) acquires a JSESSIONID on first request; if that session expires server-side while the Bearer token is still valid, subsequent requests send a stale cookie alongside the valid token, triggering a 401 that the current retry logic (which retries only connection-level errors, not 4xx) will not recover from.
A DC deployment behind a load balancer without sticky sessions can fail even on the first cross-server request if the JSESSIONID from one node is sent to another node.
findings.suggested_fix: In `build_client_from_settings`, add `options['check_update'] = False` and consider passing `get_server_info=False` to suppress the session-establishing first call that creates the JSESSIONID cookie, or document in the ADR that this is an accepted risk mitigated by PAT-per-reconcile-run (if that is the deployment model).

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add to the ADR scope (0055) a requirement to record the harness's runtime maven.atlassian.com egress dependency and that pinning the base image digest does NOT pin Jira itself — so a future maintainer can distinguish a harness design failure from an upstream artifact withdrawal (the fragility is already tracked as ticket 9895-ac7d-4276-4f08; the ADR should reference it).
evidence: tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md: 'If Atlassian ever withdraws the 8.17.1 artifacts from their public Maven repo, the harness stops working even though the base image digest above is still pinned.'

tests/external/live_jira_dc/README.md: 'Egress to maven.atlassian.com is a hard runtime dependency, not a one-time image pull. An egress-restricted or air-gapped runner cannot start this harness at all.'
Dockerfile: 'this image does NOT contain Jira. atlas-run downloads Jira ${JIRA_VERSION} (~917 artifacts) from maven.atlassian.com on first container start'
Plan AC: 'the documented commands have been executed against the J5 harness'
Evidence class: Partially-verified — the harness has been validated in CI but carries an ongoing live external dependency not flagged in the ADR scope requirements
findings.finding: The plan characterizes the Docker harness as 'the verification oracle' and the AC requires that 'documented commands have been executed against the J5 harness,' but does not flag that the harness has a hard runtime egress dependency on maven.atlassian.com (downloading ~917 artifacts at container-start, not at image-pull time). The ADR scope requires recording why the harness is the oracle — but without recording this runtime fragility, a future maintainer who finds the harness broken cannot distinguish 'Atlassian withdrew 8.17.1 artifacts' from 'the harness design is wrong.' The README records it (and it is tracked in ticket 9895-ac7d-4276-4f08), but the ADR scope as written does not require the ADR to record it.
findings.location: Approach section: 'the Docker harness as the verification oracle'; Scope: docs/adr/0055-jira-family-sub-seam.md
scenarios: A future maintainer reads the ADR to understand whether the DC oracle is still viable and finds no mention of the maven.atlassian.com dependency; they assume a pinned Docker image digest is sufficient to reproduce the oracle and are surprised when the container fails to boot.
Atlassian deprecates or rate-limits maven.atlassian.com access, breaking the harness silently — the ADR provides no guidance on whether this is expected or how to recover.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to the ADR scope's harness description: 'Record that the harness downloads Jira 8.17.1 from maven.atlassian.com at container-start (not image-pull) time, that egress to that host is a hard runtime dependency, and that fragility is tracked as ticket 9895-ac7d-4276-4f08.' This is already documented in the README; the ADR should reference it so the oracle's known limitations are visible from the architecture record.

findings.finding: J8 asserts 'FIFTEEN distinct transport members' the core reaches for, but J9's authoritative description (the ticket whose evidence the ADR is required to record) states 'the core reaches for twenty-one distinct transport members.' The number J8 cites is also internally inconsistent: 15 total - 12 absent = 3 declared, but TicketTransport visibly declares 6. The correct figures from J9's final corrected audit are 21 distinct / 12 absent / 6 declared on TicketTransport.
findings.location: Approach section — '`TicketTransport` declares SIX members while the core reaches for FIFTEEN distinct transport members; TWELVE were absent from the DC transport'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace 'the core reaches for FIFTEEN distinct transport members; TWELVE were absent from the DC transport and declared on no Protocol at all' with 'the core reaches for TWENTY-ONE distinct transport members; TWELVE were absent from the DC transport and declared on no Protocol at all' (source: J9 ticket bda8-370d, comment 2, corrected audit). Also update the corresponding AC line that currently reads '(6 declared vs 15 called, 12 absent)' to '(6 declared vs 21 called, 12 absent from DC and undeclared on the port)'.
